# Recreation Prompt

Create a mobile-first portrait browser game called **Camp Last Gasp: Final Counselor**. Preserve the mechanics of a survival-evasion tap shooter: enemies spawn in depth and advance toward the player; tapping/clicking an enemy's projected hit box removes it and increases score; holding a large RUN button or using device motion creates retreat pressure; close-contact enemies reduce health; zero health triggers game over and restart.

Rebuild the presentation as a satirical lakeside camp slasher survival scene. The player is the final counselor using flares and flashlight timing to hold back a hockey-masked slasher. Use HUD terms `FLARES`, `NERVE`, `Breath`, and `RUN`. Make the world visible through procedural Canvas art: wet pines, cabins, lake reflection, trail perspective, rain, fog, VHS scanlines, flashlight cone, flare bursts, slash marks, and a masked machete silhouette. Optimize for portrait aspect ratios from 4:7 to 9:16 with readable overlays and reachable touch controls.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source Game Truth
The preserved source (`index_old.html`) is a browser-native mobile survival shooter/evasion loop. The player starts from an overlay, taps/clicks projected approaching enemies to remove them, holds a RUN button or uses device motion to retreat, gains one score point per successful hit, loses health when an enemy reaches close depth, and enters a game-over/restart state at zero health. It uses Canvas projection, timed spawns, a health HUD, a score HUD, feedback flashes, and mobile-scoped touch handling.

## Protected Mechanics
- Start overlay -> active play -> game over -> restart flow.
- Canvas tap/click hit detection against projected enemy hit boxes.
- Timed spawn pressure with interval shrinking as score rises.
- Enemy depth movement toward player and retreat under RUN/motion input.
- Score increments only when a pursuer is successfully hit.
- Health/nerve decreases on close-contact collision; zero ends run.
- Mobile RUN button, touch canvas, and optional device motion semantics.

## Transformable Surfaces
- Title, copy, HUD vocabulary, score label, health label, objective language.
- Enemy silhouette, hand/weapon representation, feedback particles, background, palette, typography, atmosphere, and procedural props.
- Audio tone and state feedback, provided it remains gesture-safe.

## Remixed Target
`Camp Last Gasp: Final Counselor` reframes the loop as a satirical camp slasher survival game. The player is the final counselor facing down a hockey-masked slasher through a flashlight/flare view. Score is signal flares logged, health is nerve, RUN is frantic retreat, and failure is the slasher reaching the cabin.

## Implementation Spine
Single rebuilt public `index.html`, inline CSS/JS, Canvas for procedural camp scene and pursuers, DOM for mobile HUD/overlays/controls, approved catalog Google Fonts, procedural audio only.

rankings.reasoning: The core loop is surviving escalating pursuit pressure by hitting threats and using RUN/motion retreat.
Depth-projected slashers continuously advance toward the player until repelled or they deal damage.
Canvas taps/clicks against projected hit boxes are the primary action and scoring input.
A large portrait RUN button preserves the source retreat behavior and remains touch-friendly.
